questions.stem: A protein contains carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur. Which element distinguishes proteins from carbohydrates and lipids?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and lipids contain only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. Proteins also contain nitrogen (in the amino group of every amino acid) and sometimes sulfur. The presence of nitrogen is the key distinguishing element, which is why the Biuret test for protein detects nitrogen-containing peptide bonds.

questions.stem: Two amino acids join together by a condensation reaction. What type of bond forms between them?
questions.explanation: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds through condensation reactions (releasing water). Two amino acids form a dipeptide, and many amino acids joined together form a polypeptide chain. This is distinct from glycosidic bonds (carbohydrates) and ester bonds (lipids).

questions.stem: There are 20 different amino acids used to build proteins. The human body can make 11 of them. What are the remaining 9 called, and how must they be obtained?

options.text: Non-essential amino acids; they are made from lipids
Essential amino acids; they must be obtained from the diet
Essential amino acids; they are absorbed from the air
Supplementary amino acids; they come from vitamins

questions.explanation: The 9 amino acids that the body cannot synthesise are called essential amino acids and must be obtained from dietary protein. This is why a varied diet containing different protein sources is important -- animal proteins typically contain all essential amino acids, while plant proteins may lack some.

questions.stem: A Biuret test is performed on a food sample. The solution turns from blue to purple. What does this result indicate?
questions.explanation: The Biuret test detects protein. Biuret reagent (containing copper sulfate in alkaline solution) reacts with peptide bonds in proteins, changing from blue to purple/violet. The intensity of the purple colour indicates the amount of protein present. If no protein is present, the solution stays blue.

questions.stem: A person with coeliac disease cannot eat gluten (a protein found in wheat). When they eat gluten, their immune system damages the villi in the small intestine. How would this affect their nutrition?

options.text: They would absorb too many nutrients
Damaged villi reduce the surface area for absorption, leading to nutrient deficiencies
Their stomach would produce too much acid
They would be unable to produce digestive enzymes

questions.explanation: Villi provide a large surface area for nutrient absorption in the small intestine. Damage to the villi reduces this surface area, meaning fewer nutrients (including amino acids, glucose, vitamins, and minerals) can be absorbed. This can lead to malnutrition, weight loss, and various deficiency symptoms.
